top3: Valve malfunction - partial closure/sticking of the loop valve causing flow restriction with water-hammer/cavitation-induced vibration and pressure spikes (most likely; vibration-dominant signature with electrical and thermal variables normal is typical of valve manipulation in a closed pump loop)
Pump-side hydraulic fault - incipient cavitation or impeller wear/degradation generating broadband vibration and pressure fluctuation while motor current remains normal
Instrumentation artifact - loosened accelerometer mounting or intermittent sensor fault producing spurious RMS spikes (less likely because both accelerometers and pressure co-excurse)
reasoning: The episode is abnormal: Accelerometer2RMS reaches |z|=13.56 with ~0.4% of samples beyond 3σ, and Pressure and Accelerometer1RMS also show >3σ excursions, while Current, Voltage, Thermocouple and Temperature stay within normal bounds, ruling out a motor electrical or thermal problem. The co-occurrence of large vibration spikes with pressure transients in a closed water loop, without sustained flow or current change, best matches a valve event such as partial closure or sticking that induces water hammer/cavitation. Sensor artifact is unlikely because both accelerometers correlate (r=0.468) and pressure moves with them.
